OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt.

Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit.

Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL.

## 🧠 TL;DR

1. Open a GitHub issue.
2. Describe the game or app you want.
3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue.
4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result.

```text
Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project
```

## ⚡ Quick Start

Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request:

```text
Build a neon asteroid game.

Requirements:
- Arrow-key movement
- Score and restart button
- Win and lose states
- Responsive browser layout
- Run tests and verify it in a browser
```

That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit.

To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a
`branch: <name>` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed
before the issue body is sent to OpenCode:

```sh
gh issue create \
  --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \
  --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \
  --body "Build a tiny browser page." \
  --label Goal \
  --label OpenCode
```

The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent,
the repository default branch remains the target.

## 🌍 What Can You Build?

| 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example |
|---|---|
| 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 |
| 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games |
| 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys |
| 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views |
| 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps |
| 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases |
| 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept |
| 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile |

## 🧰 What Happens Automatically?

> **The workflow is the product.**

- 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills.
- 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels.
- 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills.
- 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project.
- 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation.
- 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime.
- 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes.
- 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/<run-id>` branch.
- 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility.
- 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue.
- 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes.

## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels

Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML.

```text
model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free
skill/load-sketchfab-threejs
skill/gauntlet-loop
```

The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from:

```text
.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
```

# Testing and verification

## Use the preconfigured Linux CLI

Run `scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh` on an Ubuntu worker to install the pinned
CLI, Chromium, Mesa Vulkan drivers, and a persistent Xvfb display. Let the reusable
workflow run this before publishing SSH access. Use `playwright-cli` from Actions
or a fresh SSH shell; let the wrapper supply DISPLAY and the Linux configuration.
Use `playwright-cli -s=check open <url>`, `eval`, `screenshot`, and `close` without
manual browser flags. Load `.github/templates/linux.md` by default. Select `mac.md` instead when
a `mac` label or `#mac` hashtag is present. Match case insensitively. Recheck the actual screenshot after upgrades.

## Capture the Linux WebGPU triangle

Install Playwright 1.63.0 and its full Chromium browser as below. Install
`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve
`tests/fixtures/webgpu-triangle.html` over localhost HTTP. Run:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-runtime xvfb-run -a node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/webgpu-triangle.html --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --backend swiftshader --require-green-triangle --out /tmp/linux-triangle
```

Require green triangle pixels, a usable device, `scene.webgpu.rendered=true`,
and no page errors. Inspect the image. Treat SwiftShader and Mesa llvmpipe as
CPU rendering, not GPU hardware acceleration. Use the headed Xvfb result on
[run 34908797646](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/actions/runs/34908797646)
as the verified 2026-09-15 reference. Do not accept the headless result from
that run: its initial generic pixel check falsely accepted background pixels.
Retain the fixture's GPU reference. Preserve failed diagnostics when investigating
`A valid external Instance reference no longer exists`. Do not infer a single
root cause from the combined driver-installation and fixture changes.
Use `--backend vulkan` for native-driver experiments, `--backend swangle` for
ANGLE SwiftShader experiments, and `--executable` to select another browser.
Keep the default Metal path for the Mac test.

## Capture Pascal Editor on Linux

Use `http://localhost:3002`, not the numeric loopback origin, with the default
Pascal Next.js development server. Check the server log for blocked development
resources when HTTP 403 or HMR handshake errors occur.
Install dependencies with the repository's Bun lockfile. Start `bun dev` and
wait for the editor on port 3002. Create a studio through `POST /api/scenes`
using the documented scene structure. Open `/scene/<id>?disable=postFx` for
the reduced-effects capture. Do not use the empty root page as a scene test.
Run headed Chromium under Xvfb with the tested SwiftShader flags above.
Wait for visible geometry; verify the existing canvas accepts `webgpu` and
rejects `webgl2`. Require the viewer's `WebGPU device ready` log, no failed
HTTP requests, and no JavaScript errors. Inspect the screenshot manually.
Treat the 2026-09-15 room capture on issue 113 as a software-rendering result.
Do not claim full post-processing coverage. Preserve readiness-timeout warnings
in the report; do not confuse an earlier WebGL fallback capture with the final
WebGPU capture. Keep the saved scene and application server for further tests.

## Capture WebGPU on a hosted Mac

Use full Chromium with the Metal backend. Keep Playwright's other launch defaults. Test
headed mode first; use `--headless` only after comparing the actual captures.
Install Playwright and its full Chromium build in a separate runtime directory:

```sh
npm install --prefix /tmp/gpu-capture-runtime playwright@1.63.0
/tmp/gpu-capture-runtime/node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-capture-runtime node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/ --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --require-metal --out /tmp/game-capture
```

Replace the URL and canvas selector with the running game's values. Start the
game before capture if it requires user input. Read `diagnostic.json`,
`canvas.png`, and `page.png` from the output directory. Require an available
WebGPU device, no page errors, and painted canvas pixels. Exclude CSS borders
from the pixel check. Accept a flat triangle with two interior colours; reject
a uniform interior even when its border has another colour.

Use `--baseline` to test full Chromium without extra flags. Use `--headless`
to test the same full browser headlessly. Do not substitute the separate
headless shell. Preserve failed diagnostics; do not silently skip absent
adapters. Keep Vulkan flags out of the macOS Metal capture path.

Use the verified flags: `--enable-gpu`, `--ignore-gpu-blocklist`,
`--enable-unsafe-webgpu`, and `--use-angle=metal`. Check `chrome://gpu` in a
separate headed page. Interpret `Apple Paravirtual device` as a virtual Metal

## Objective
- Build a polished 2D top-down sci-fi game blending Stardew Valley–style farming with colony building, featuring multiple colonizable planets starting with one solar system.
- User request (Portuguese): "Jogo 2D top-down de ficção científica misturado com estilo de Stardew Valley e construção de colônia. E faça outros planetas para colonizar começando com um sistema solar"

## Requirements
- Browser-playable 2D top-down game, responsive for desktop/mobile.
- Stardew-like farming plus sci-fi colony construction.
- Multiple colonizable planets within a solar system.
- UI in Portuguese (pt-BR).
- Must run from static `index.html` via the existing runtime; no framework/build requirement.
- Capture flow auto-clicks a button whose accessible label matches exactly `Play`; primary title button uses `aria-label="Play"`.

## Decisions
- Single static HTML/CSS/JS app with ES modules under `src/`.
- Five-planet system "Aurora": Nix (start), Cinder, Verdant, Frost, Aether.
- Mechanics chosen: tilling/watering/planting/harvesting, resource nodes, day/night, colonist economy, buildings, research-gated travel, beacon-based planet claiming, quests, autosave/localStorage, synthesized WebAudio.
- Renderer: Canvas 2D with procedural cached terrain, generated astronaut sprites, procedural buildings/particles/weather/title art, DOM HUD overlays.
- No package.json (keeps runtime static-server path working); Node tests can run with `--experimental-default-type=module`.
- Three starter plots pre-placed on Nix; first plot should be changed to fully grown (`growth: 1`) for immediate visual payoff.

## Work State

### Completed
- `index.html`: full title screen, HUD, resource bar, quest/colony panels, hotbar, build/map/help/pause overlays, travel panel, touch controls.
- `styles.css`: complete visual system, glass/neon panels, responsive layouts, animations.
- `src/config.js`: planets, crops, buildings, tools, node types, quests, starter resources.
- `src/rng.js`: deterministic hash/noise/mulberry helpers.
- `src/world.js`: terrain generation, node scatter, starter setup, collision/placement helpers.
- `src/sim.js`: state creation, economy ticks, crop growth, tool actions, quests, travel/unlock helpers, save restore.
- `src/sprites.js`: generated 4-direction/4-frame astronaut.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized ambient music and SFX.
- `src/save.js`: localStorage save/load wrappers.
- `src/render.js`: world/title rendering, plots, crops, nodes, buildings, player/drone, particles, night/day, weather, vignette.
- `src/map.js`: animated solar-system map with planet selection, locks, claimed status, travel ship animation.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD updates, hotbar/seed picker, toasts, build cards, map side panel, help/pause/title wiring, touch joystick.
- `src/sim.js` patched to include `state.player` on new game.

### Active
- `src/main.js` still needs to be written (game loop, input, camera, interactions, build/travel/pause flow, toasts, autosave).
- Runtime/browser verification not yet performed.
- Tests not yet written.
- README still only contains OMGithub boilerplate.

### Blocked
- Nothing external; main integration file remains before the app can load.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` implementing the `Game` class expected by `ui.js`/`map.js`: constructor, `newGame`, `continueGame`, `returnToTitle`, `resetGame`, loop/update/render, camera, movement/collision, mouse/aim/hover info, tool use, build ghost/placement, travel, overlays, sound, autosave, quest/unlock notifications.
2. Set starter plot growth to `1` in `src/world.js` (`starterSetup`) so the first crop is ripe/glowing on load.
3. Add `tests/core.test.mjs` and run `node --experimental-default-type=module --test tests/core.test.mjs`.
4. Start static server on `PORT=3000` via `./start.sh` in tmux; verify with `playwright-cli` (headed/Xvfb) at `http://localhost:3000`, click `Play`, screenshot desktop/mobile, inspect for errors/blank canvas.
5. Fix runtime issues found, then update README with game description/controls.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/main.js`: missing integration entry point; highest priority.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/ui.js`: expects many `Game` methods/properties; use as integration contract.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/sim.js`: core state/economy/actions/save logic; `state.player` added.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/render.js`: renderer reads `game.camera`, `game.clock`, `game.aimTile`, `game.buildGhost`, `game.drone`, `game.particles`, `game.floats`, `game.state.player`.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/map.js`: reads `game.travelAnim`, calls `game.selectPlanet`.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/world.js`: terrain/collision/placement; adjust starter crop ripeness.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/src/config.js`: all tuned data.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/index.html`: DOM ids/classes used by UI.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/styles.css`: UI styling/responsive behavior.
- `/home/runner/work/Colonia2D/Colonia2D/README.md`: needs project documentation.

## Important Context
- Current git state: only initial commit `2f7df5c`; all created game files are uncommitted/untracked.
- Game is served statically by `$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs` on `PORT` (default 3000) when no `package.json` exists; do not add `package.json` or replace `start.sh`.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

# Colônia Aurora

Um jogo 2D top-down de fazenda espacial e construção de colônia, jogável direto no navegador. Cultive o impossível, monte uma base autossuficiente e expanda a humanidade por cinco mundos do sistema Aurora.

![Colônia Aurora](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-jogável-6ee7ff?style=for-the-badge)

## O que tem no jogo

- **Fazenda no espaço:** prepare canteiros, regue, plante e colha lumifrutas, trigo estelar e criobagas.
- **Construção de colônia:** habitats, painéis solares, extratores de água, estufas, oficinas, laboratórios, plataformas de pouso e faróis de colonização.
- **Economia viva:** colonos consomem água e alimento, geram créditos e aumentam a produção. A felicidade afeta o rendimento de cada ciclo.
- **Cinco planetas:** Nix (início), Cinder, Verdant, Frost e Aether, cada um com bioma, modificadores, recursos e arte procedural próprios.
- **Pesquisa e rotas:** laboratórios geram pesquisa; pesquisa e colônias desbloqueiam viagens interestelares.
- **Reivindicação de mundos:** em planetas virgens, construa um Farol de Colonização para fundar uma nova colônia.
- **Ciclo dia/noite, clima, partículas e áudio sintetizado:** tudo gerado no navegador, sem assets externos.
- **Progressão guiada:** 11 diretrizes, recompensas, notificações e salvamento automático local.

## Como jogar

| Ação | Teclado | Toque |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mover | WASD / setas | Joystick virtual |
| Usar ferramenta | E / Espaço | Botão **E** |
| Trocar semente | Q | Seletor de sementes |
| Selecionar ferramenta | 1–6 | Barra de equipamento |
| Construir | B | Botão **CONSTRUIR** |
| Mapa estelar | M | Botão **MAPA** |
| Ajuda | H | Botão de ajuda |
| Pausa / fechar menu | Esc | Botão de menu |
| Som | F | Botão de som |

### Primeiros passos

1. Use a **enxada** em solo livre para preparar canteiros.
2. Regue e plante sementes. Plantas maduras brilham em dourado.
3. Colha para obter alimento, créditos e novas sementes.
4. Abra **CONSTRUIR** e erga um Habitat e um Painel Solar.
5. Colete cristais, sucata, gelo e flora pelo terreno.
6. Pesquise no Laboratório, abra o **MAPA** e viaje para Cinder.
7. Em um mundo novo, construa o **Farol de Colonização**.

## Executar localmente

O projeto é estático, sem etapa de build e sem dependências de runtime.

```bash
./start.sh
# abre em http://localhost:3000
```

Se preferir qualquer servidor estático:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000
```

## Testes

Os testes de simulação usam o runner nativo do Node:

```bash
node --experimental-default-type=module --test tests/core.test.mjs
```

## Estrutura

```text
index.html          telas, HUD e overlines
styles.css          sistema visual e responsividade
src/config.js       planetas, culturas, estruturas, missões e balanceamento
src/world.js        terreno procedural, colisão e posicionamento
src/sim.js          estado, economia, ações, missões, viagem e save
src/render.js       renderização do mundo e da tela-título
src/map.js          mapa estelar animado
src/ui.js           HUD, menus, toasts e controles de toque
src/audio.js        música e efeitos sintetizados via WebAudio
src/save.js         persistência em localStorage
src/main.js         loop principal, câmera e integração
tests/core.test.mjs testes da simulação
```

## Objective
- Build a polished browser-playable 2D top-down sci-fi game blending Stardew Valley–style farming with colony building, including multiple colonizable planets starting with one solar system.

## Requirements
- Browser-playable 2D top-down game, responsive for desktop and mobile.
- Stardew-like farming plus sci-fi colony construction.
- Multiple colonizable planets within a solar system.
- UI in Portuguese (pt-BR).
- Must run from static `index.html`; no framework/build requirement.
- Capture flow auto-clicks a visible, enabled button whose accessible label matches exactly `Play`; primary title button uses `aria-label="Play"`.

## Decisions
- Single static HTML/CSS/JS app with ES modules under `src/`.
- Five-planet system "Aurora": Nix (start), Cinder, Verdant, Frost, Aether.
- Mechanics: tilling/watering/planting/harvesting, resource nodes, day/night, colonist economy, buildings, research-gated travel, beacon-based planet claiming, quests, autosave/localStorage, synthesized WebAudio.
- Renderer: Canvas 2D with procedural cached terrain, generated astronaut sprites, procedural buildings/particles/weather/title art, DOM HUD overlays.
- No `package.json`; Node tests run with `--experimental-default-type=module`.
- Three starter plots pre-placed on Nix; first plot now starts fully grown (`growth: 1`).
- Beacon now grants `cap: 1` so a newly claimed planet shows `1/1` population instead of `1/0`.
- Button hover feedback changed from `transform` to `filter` to reduce capture actionability instability.

## Work State

### Completed
- `src/main.js` implemented: game loop, input, camera, collision, tool use, build/travel/pause/map/help flow, particles, autosave, notifications, save/continue/reset.
- `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/config.js`, `src/rng.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/sim.js`, `src/sprites.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/save.js`, `src/render.js`, `src/map.js`, `src/ui.js` are implemented.
- Fixed renderer integration bug by calling `renderer.drawWorld(this, dt)` instead of passing `state`.
- Added responsive mobile resource-bar wrapping so all six resource chips remain visible; adjusted toast offset.
- Added `tests/core.test.mjs`; all 11 tests pass:
  `node --experimental-default-type=module --test tests/core.test.mjs`
- Browser-verified title, gameplay, harvesting, building, claiming, travel, save/continue, map, pause, help, build overlay, and mobile layout.
- README rewritten with game description, controls, mechanics, local run/test commands, and file structure.
- Static server running in tmux session `colonia` on `http://localhost:3000`.
- Capture succeeded once for both desktop and mobile after hover-transform fix.

- Investigating intermittent desktop capture failure: `Capture desktop: auto-start not-actionable`.
- Repeated `CAPTURE_STRICT=1 ./capture.sh` run had desktop fail and mobile succeed.
